results.title: How Tariffs Are Affecting the PCB Circuit Board Industry – EMSG Inc.
results.content:
At present, there is a 10% universal tariff on most goods imported to the U.S. However, individual nations and specific goods have also been targeted with their own specific tariffs based on the status of their trade relationship. Japanese cars, for instance, face a 25% tariff. At the moment, there are no U.S. tariffs on printed circuit board imports specifically. However, imported PCBs and their components and materials are still subjected to both the universal 10% tariff and the tariffs [...] China — the largest producer of PCBs in the world — has been the primary target of the administration’s tariffs. As such, imported goods from China currently face the highest country-specific tariff rates of any nation in the world, with the average imported good facing a 30% tariff at the very least. However, even this lowered tariff rate may not last, as it is the result of a 90-day trade agreement between the U.S. and China. [...] Other PCB-producing nations that have been targeted with tariffs include:

PCB components and materials have also been affected by tariffs. Mexico — a key producer of connectors, sub-assemblies and PCBs — has been hit with 25% tariffs on all goods not compliant with the Agreement between the United States of America, the United Mexican States, and Canada (USMCA). Imported copper, which many PCB manufacturers rely on, is also facing a 25% tariff rate.

results.title: PCB Tariffs from China to the US in 2026: HTS Codes, Section 301, and Landed Cost
results.content:
Section 301 tariffs apply in addition to the normal HTS duty rate. For many China-origin bare PCBs under HTS 8534.00 and certain PCBAs under HTS 8473.30.1180, the additional Section 301 tariff is 25% unless a product-specific exclusion applies.

Use this table as a planning reference only, not as a final classification decision. Verify current rates with your customs broker before placing any order. [...] US PCB imports from China face HTS classification (8534 bare PCBs, 8473 PCBAs) and possible 25% Section 301 tariff. Landed cost = FOB + freight + duty + fees. Exclusions limited; de minimis not reliable in 2026. [...] For PCB buyers, the most relevant exclusion to check is HTS 9903.88.69. Current Federal Register materials extend certain Section 301 exclusions through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on November 9, 2026. Some qualifying two-layer and four-layer rigid PCBs may fall under this exclusion when they match the product description precisely.

results.title: Tariffs on Electronics from China: 2025 Guide for Purchasers
results.content:
### Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs)

Tariffs on rigid and flex PCBs sourced from China typically range from 25% to 30%. This means higher costs for prototyping and production alike, complicating budgeting during early-stage design and putting pressure on already tight development cycles.

### Electronic Components [...] As of June 2025, the U.S. government has sweeping tariffs on a wide range of Chinese imports, including a broad spectrum of electronics. Tariff rates on these products now commonly fall between 10% and 40%, depending on classification, and are part of a broader campaign to stimulate domestic manufacturing, reinforce trade leverage, and respond to long-standing intellectual property concerns. [...] In some cases, importing bare PCBs or semi-finished subassemblies and completing assembly or testing in the U.S. or Mexico can significantly reduce the import duty on electronics from China.

While domestic labor may cost more, the duty savings and reduced customs risk can make this approach financially viable, particularly in sensitive product categories, like PCBs, power management systems, and medical device subassemblies.
